captions.text: A computer works in three stages: input, processing and output.
Input devices send data into the computer. They are how we give the computer instructions.
The keyboard lets us type letters, numbers and commands.
The mouse moves the pointer on the screen, so we can point, click and select.
A microphone turns our voice and other sounds into data the computer can store.
A webcam captures pictures and video, for example in an online class.
Inside the system unit, the CPU processes the data and turns it into information.
Output devices give that information back to us, in a form we can see, hear or hold.
The monitor shows text, pictures and video. It is soft copy output.
The printer puts information onto paper. This is called hard copy.
Speakers play sound, like music and voices.
Input goes in, processing happens inside, and output comes out. Now sort each device yourself.
